main_text.l: אבנט m. Balteus, Levit.8.13. Aff. וַאֲבְנֵטְךָ Et balteo tuo, Jes.22.21. Plur. אַבְנֵטִים Exod.28.40.
אָבַס Saginare: Particip. Pahul, אָבוּס Saginatus, Prov.15.17. Plur. אֲבוּסִים 1.Reg.4.23.
אבוס m. Præsepe, quasi Saginatorium: בְּאֵין אֲלָפִים אָבוּס בָּהּ Cùm non fuerint boves, præsepe mundum est, Proverb.14.4. Plural. cum Affix. אֲבוּסֶיךָ Præsepia tua, Job.39.12.
מַאֲבוּסִים m.p. Granaria: Aff. מַאֲבְסֵיהָ Granaria, Horrea ejus, Jer.50.26.
אָבָק m. Pulvis, Pulvisculus: Constr. אֲבַק רַגְלָיו Pulvis pedum ejus, Nah.1.3. Aff. אֲבָקָם Pulvis eo-rum, Ezech.26.10.
אַבְקַת f. Idem: unde Constr. מִכֹּל אַבְקַת רוֹכֵל Præ omni pulvere aromatarii, Cant.3.6.

יֵאָבֵק Niph. Luctari, quòd hoc in pulvere fieret: Unde, Fulvâ luctantur arenâ, apud Virgil. Et, In arenam de-scendere. Futurum, וַיֵּאָבֵק Et luctatus est, Gen.32.24. Infin. cum Aff. בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ In luctando ipsum, Gen.32.25.
אָבִיר m. Robustus, Fortis, Potens, Validus: Constr. אֲבִיר יַעֲקֹב Robustus Jacobi,Gen.49.24. אֲבִיר יִשְׂרָאֵל Fortis Israelis, Jes.1.24. Apud Rabbinos, אבר Roborare, Obfirmare.

אֲבִיר m. Idem: כַּאֲבִיר Ut potentissimus, Jesa.10.13. pro כַּאֲבִיר, & juxta Masorethas legendū כָּבִיר. Plur. אֲבִירִים Robusti: Synecdochicè Tauri, Juvenci, Equi, quòd hu[?] Robur competat: unde, Fortes invertant tauri, apud Virgil. Et, Non fortitudine equi delectatur, Psal.147.10. Const. אֲבִירֵי בָשָׁן Robusti juvenci Baschanis, Psal.22.13. Aff. אֲבִירַי Fortes meos, Thren.1.15.
אֵבֶר m. Penna, Ala, quòd in iis Robur avium sit: אֵבֶר כְּיוֹנָה Alas quasi columba, Psal.55.7.

page.notes: Hebrew vocalisation and some Hebrew forms are copied as far as legible at this resolution; the vowel points, especially in the Constr./Aff. forms, may be imperfect. "hu[?]" at the line end of the entry אֲבִיר is unclear. The Latin "Præ" (entry אַבְקַת) and "Obfirmare" are printed as they appear. No notes or marginal text on the page.
